Folks — looping in proposed legal-friendly language and operational guardrails below (draft to present on the call). I pulled the most friction points from both redlines and made concrete compromise wording.

1) Measurement window
- Proposed: Monthly availability percentage calculated as (Total minutes available per calendar month / Total minutes in the month) * 100.
- Rationale: preserves smoothing but still compatible with calendar constraints; if BlueBox needs per-customer calendar-day measurement, we can add a defined exception schedule and list the affected customers in the Order Form appendix.

2) Scheduled maintenance
- Proposed: Redwood may conduct scheduled maintenance up to once per week for up to 4 hours, with at least 72 hours' prior notice.
- Short-notice security patches: Redwood may perform urgent maintenance with minimum 12 hours' notice where a material security vulnerability is confirmed; Redwood will provide a post-action report within 48 hours.

3) Service credit calculation and cap
- Proposed: For monthly availability below thresholds, credit = (Threshold - Actual) / Threshold * Monthly Fee. Cap at 30% of the Monthly Fee for critical enterprise accounts; 25% default cap for standard accounts.

4) Escalation and response times (for support incidents)
- P0 (Platform down): initial response <= 15 minutes, active remediation updates every 30 minutes until mitigated.
- P1 (major feature impact): initial response <= 1 hour, updates every 4 hours.

5) Emergency maintenance carve-out and auditability
- Redwood will maintain an audit log of maintenance events and provide access to logs for designated BlueBox contacts upon request.

I'll put these as tracked changes in the order form before the call. If you want, Dev can confirm ops-level feasibility on the call.

-Laura

Thanks everyone — quick consolidation from Redwood ahead of today's sync:

- Measurement: We accept the Monthly availability calculation as base case. If BlueBox needs per-customer calendar-day measurement for named regulated customers, we'll add an appendix listing those customers (agreed exception).

- Scheduled maintenance: 1x/week up to 4 hours with 72 hours notice. Redwood accepts a 12-hour short-notice carve-out limited to confirmed critical security patches; Redwood will publish a post-action report within 48 hours.

- Service credits: Redwood will accept a 30% cap on monthly credits for identified critical enterprise accounts (we'll list these in the Order Form appendix). Standard accounts retain a 25% cap. Credit calculation will follow Laura's formula.

- Response times & escalation: P0 <=15m initial; P1 <=1h initial. Will include escalation contact list (Ops + Account).
